answer_core:
Do not confront the partner, investigate privately, access systems unusually, or pick a reporting channel yourself. Tonight, write down exactly what you saw, preserve your own notes, tell your spouse in broad strokes, and contact two or three whistleblower attorneys.

Counsel first does not mean blind deference. During intake, ask practical questions that reveal channel bias: when have they advised internal-first, audit-committee-first, or external-first, and why? Let counsel review the facts and choose the safest path.

Attend Wednesday normally. If the partner raises the encounter, keep the response narrow: do not deny, elaborate, confront, investigate, or be alone with the partner if avoidable. Fear can push premature filing or paralysis, so keep the first moves reversible.
